claims.statement: Strategy to pursue growth with profitability
Target combined ratio of 110% and ROE around 10% over medium term (2-3 years)
Aim for double-digit premium growth of around 10% overall
Strive to distribute 30% of PAT as dividend
Rationalized office count from 2100+ to 1840 in India via tier restructuring; ongoing viability analysis
Digital penetration currently ~12% of overall business; targeting increase via portals and claim digitization
Gross written premium grew 8.3% to INR 41,996 crores; market share 12.78%
Combined ratio 120.99% vs 117% prior year; ICR 97.36% vs 95.59%; expense ratio 14.89%
Focus on retail segment and better performance expected in coming quarters
Target double-digit ROE in short to medium term (1-3 years)
Plan to bring down combined ratio significantly in medium term
Combined ratio at 116.05% for Q1 FY25 vs 115.16% YoY
Incurred claim ratio improved to 95.98% in Q1 FY25 from 96.19% YoY
GWP Rs 11,788 crore in Q1 FY25; net earned premium Rs 8,503 crore, up 7.37% YoY
Market share 14.67% as of June 30, 2024; remain market leader
Investing heavily in systems, processes, skill development; inducted risk engineers, automobile engineers, doctors
Company expects profitability trend to improve in coming quarters
Management expects gross premium growth of around 10% by end of FY25 from current sub-3% level
Medium-term growth target of 12-15% over next 2-3 years as organizational restructuring impact fades
Internal target to achieve combined ratio of 105-107% within next 2-3 years
Goal to achieve combined ratio within 105% in next two years
Incurred claims ratio improved to 98.92% for H1 FY25 from 101.03% in H1 FY24
Combined ratio improved to 120.55% for H1 FY25 from 122.68% in H1 FY24
Expense ratio reduced from 13.13% to 12.43% year-on-year for half year
Commission ratio increased to 9.41% from 8.82% due to market competition for agent and broker commissions
Fire segment incurred claims ratio dropped significantly from 98% to 77%
Motor TP incurred claims ratio increased due to no pricing hikes in 2-3 years, higher court awards and interest costs
Senior citizen retail health policies have loss ratio of 117-122%
Retail health loss ratio is less than 100%
Investing in digital initiatives including automation of simple products, digital claims servicing up to Rs 1 lakh, and anti-fraud software
Recruited automobile engineers for auto hubs and conducting ongoing recruitment for more automobile engineers
Hired medical officers for claims processing and expanding PPN network in tier 2 and tier 3 cities
CMD: Q3 FY25 PAT Rs 641 Cr; GWP growth muted at 2.4% due to non-renewal of inadequate large accounts
CMD: Combined ratio for quarter ended Dec 2024 was 116.33%; solvency improved to 1.90x in Dec 2024 from 1.81x in Sep 2024
CMD: Renewed Rajasthan govt health scheme covering ~1.3 Cr families from Feb 2025 with ~20% per-family premium increase
CMD: Property segment premium hardening seen in Q4 FY25; overall growth momentum expected better going forward
Expect robust recovery in growth momentum during Q4 FY25 supported by premium strengthening in property insurance and profitable underwriting
Confident of achieving solvency ratio of 2x in near future
Combined ratio improved to 119.08% for 9M FY25 from 120.34% in 9M FY24
Q3 FY25 combined ratio at 116.33% reflecting steady progress in managing claims and controlling expenses
Motor TP incurred claim ratio on earned premium rose to 88.94% in 9M FY25 from 83.05% in FY24 due to non-revision of premium by Ministry of Road Transport
Health segment incurred claim ratio improved substantially to 103.25% overall with retail at 88%, group health at 103%, government at 114%
Gross written premium reached INR32,186 crores with net earned premium of INR26,061 crores as of December 31, 2024
Fire segment premium declined 9.08% while all other segments showed positive growth
Rationalizing operating offices, increasing digital penetration, leveraging technology for customer satisfaction and profitability
Net incurred claim ratio improved to 96.61% in FY25 from 97.36% in FY24
Expense ratio improved to 10.21% in FY25 from 13.78% in FY24
Combined ratio improved to 116.78% in FY25 from 119.88% in FY24
Solvency ratio improved to 1.91 in FY25 from 1.81 in FY24
Return on equity was 4.66% in FY25 vs 5.58% in FY24
Management targets combined ratio of 110% in near future
Motor TP ICR 108.2% vs 96.4% prior year; awaiting premium revision from government/regulator
Health & PA ICR improved to 100.9% from 105.9% prior year
Excluding Motor TP, ICR improved to 94.2% from 97.6% prior year
Invested Rs 5 crore in Bima Sugam India Federation equity via private placement
Management targets combined ratio improvement of 3% to around 113% for FY26
Combined ratio stable at 116.16% in Q1 FY26 vs 116.13% in Q1 FY25
Net incurred claims ratio increased to 99.76% from 95.98% due to aviation and health claims
Expense ratio reduced to 7.86% from 11.65% driven by negative net employee addition
Management has no visibility on motor TP price hike timing this financial year
Adding 50 direct recruit doctors to existing 75 for health claim audits
Motor TP ICR improved to 105.09% from 111.71% due to portfolio mix shift toward private cars
Motor OD ICR increased to 116.35% from 114.86% due to OEM and dealer commission pressure
Company outpaced industry growth in October 2025; loss ratios expected to improve in H2FY26
IFRS 17 implementation mandated from 1st April 2027 with parallel run in FY27
Risk-based capital framework expected to be rolled out shortly by regulator
Combined ratio equivalent under IFRS 17 will improve but exact quantum not quantified
Retail health target 30% of book in near term, 50% long-term
Net Incurred Claim Ratio 104.22% in H1 FY26 vs 99.22% in H1 FY25
Combined ratio 127.21% in H1 FY26 vs 120% in H1 FY25
Expense ratio 13.64% in H1 FY26 vs 11.67% in H1 FY25 due to wage revision provision
Profit After Tax up 57.7% YoY to Rs 454 crores in H1 FY26
One-time wage revision provision of Rs 1,680 crores impacted expense ratio and combined ratio
Excluding wage revision provision, operating expenses have come down due to office optimization and negative net employee addition
Solvency ratio 1.79x in H1 FY26 vs 1.81x in H1 FY25
Target double-digit ROE by reducing incurred claim ratio
Health loss ratio target 98-100%, Motor loss ratio target 103-104%
Motor growth to turn positive in next couple of quarters with new dealer partnerships
FPS provision of Rs 700-800 crore to be taken in Q4 FY26 after notification
Long-term tax rate expected at 17.42% MAT rate from FY27
Q3 FY26 combined ratio 117.98%, 9M FY26 combined ratio 124%
Q3 FY26 combined ratio ex-wage revision 110.13%, 9M FY26 ex-wage revision 117.6%
Q3 FY26 net incurred claim ratio 90.77%, down from 94.49% YoY
Health ICR improved from 103% to 91% in Q3, 9M from 103% to 101%
Motor ICR worsened to 108% in Q3 from 102% YoY due to portfolio cleanup
Fire ICR worsened to 65% in Q3 from 54% YoY, 9M at 81%
Marine ICR 119% in Q3 due to large ship sinking claims
Aviation ICR 149% in Q3 due to Air India claim, 9M at 323%
Engineering ICR improved to 3% in Q3 from 37% YoY
Liability ICR improved to 21% in Q3 from 57% YoY
Investing in fraud monitoring software, vendor selection underway, expected in 3-4 months
Increased health inspections from 30% to 50% compulsorily, hiring more doctors
CMD remains optimistic about growth prospects in FY27 with focus on retail and MSME segments
FY27 industry growth expected double-digit; New India domestic growth double-digit; Motor growth single-digit
FY26 combined ratio 122.57% including wage revision; adjusted combined ratio 116.67% vs 115.34% prior year
FY26 gross domestic premium INR 42,822 crores, up 10.9% YoY; market share 12.74%
IT infrastructure revamp nearing completion; digital marketing and sales piloted for Health products; mobile super apps for customers, intermediaries, surveyors implemented; AI/ML tools in daily use
Industry property premium crashed 27.8% in Q1 FY27; Motor TP under pressure with no premium increase and claim inflation
Focus on changing business mix toward retail and MSME with newer product lines where competitive intensity is lower
